text: answer[mkt-1788836084764-29cc05]: Title: Whether We're Living in a Simulation — The Math Actually Does Check Out (and it's disturbing) Top comment (u/pseudoscience_pete, 4.2k upvotes): Look, I know Nick Bostrom's paper keeps getting recycled but the original argument is actually tighter than people realize. You don't need aliens or a literal computer — you just need three assumptions: civilizations don't all go extinct before going spacefaring, they eventually run ancestor simulations, and the number of simulated minds vastly outnumbers the number of biological ones. If even one of those is true for even one civilization, the odds that you're the original are basically zero. What unsettles me isn't the simulation hypothesis itself — it's that the argument doesn't actually give you anything actionable. You can't "optimize" your way out of the code. You can't message the server. It just means every person you've ever loved might be a render in someone else's GPU cluster, and you'd never know the difference.
